rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted, rules the universe from His throne, and is inaccessible to creatures.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has an exalted status and is the master of the

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters' supposed divine associates are invented by them and have no basis.
rows.anchor: The deities whom these idolaters have regarded as His associates and favoured ones have only been invented by them and have no basis.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He interprets al-rūḥ as divine revelation, which gives the heart and intellect life, warmth, and light, like the spirit animating the body; he cites Jesus' saying in Matthew 4:4.
rows.anchor: divine revelation gives life, warmth and light to the heart and intellect.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'from His command' marks revelation as a divine matter whose full nature is known only to its sender or recipient.
rows.anchor: Only he understands it who sends it or he who experiences it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans and jinn cannot access God's secrets; revelation to messengers is the sole way to know His will, making the idolaters' eavesdropping claims baseless.
rows.anchor: The only way to know of God’s likes and dislikes is divine revelation, which the Almighty sends down to His messengers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chooses messengers whom He deems worthy; not every claimant is fit for the position.
rows.anchor: God selects for this position whomsoever He wants, and the one He selects really deserves to be selected; not every claimant is worthy of it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters' pride makes them think a messenger should come from among themselves.
rows.anchor: Their over-weaning pride has led them to conclude that if God was to make someone as His messenger, he should have been from among them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-talaq means the Day of Judgment, when everyone appears before the Lord; warning about it is revelation's and prophethood's central purpose, and the messengers guide people toward it.
rows.anchor: The real purpose of divine revelation and prophethood is to inform people of this Day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every person's inner and outer self will be exposed before God, leaving no need for witnesses, evidence, excuses, lies, or false recommendations.
rows.anchor: The inner and outer self of every person will be exposed before God on that Day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question of who rules today challenges idolaters to say where the intercessors and deities they expected to save them have gone.
rows.anchor: Where are those intercessors and deities which these idolaters had set up as partners of God and thought that they would save them from God?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers that sovereignty belongs to Him alone, the One and Almighty; no one can be another's friend or alter His decision.
rows.anchor: no one will be able to be a friend to another nor be able to change a decision of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment will fully manifest God's justice: each person receives recompense for deeds without injustice, and the reckoning is immediate.
rows.anchor: none will be wronged or treated unjustly and all this will happen in the blink of an eye.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-āzifa means something that has come near and names the approaching Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: means “that which has come near.” Here it is used for the Day of Judgement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites the saying that a person's judgment begins at death; no source grading is given in the passage.
rows.anchor: he who dies, his day of judgement has arrived

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elapsed time after death will feel so short that each person will think they only just slept and awoke; death and the Day are near.
rows.anchor: each person will think that he had just slept a while ago and now woken up.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a nation that rejects its messenger, the approaching divine verdict brings destruction as a lesser judgment before the final Judgment; this warns Quraysh not to think the Day is distant.
rows.anchor: This destruction is like a lesser day of judgement which is like a prelude to the greater day of judgement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of hearts reaching throats depicts sinners' terror and grief; they cannot speak in their defense and have no sympathizer or advocate.
rows.anchor: it will be as if the hearts of the sinners have reached their throats, and they will be stricken with grief and sorrow

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qualifying 'intercessor' with 'whose plea is heeded' refutes the idolaters' belief that their favored deities' pleas must be accepted.
rows.anchor: to refute a claim of the idolaters

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession helps only when a judge lacks the full facts; God knows every person's secrets, including furtive glances and what hearts conceal, so no recommendation can sway Him.
rows.anchor: He even has knowledge of furtive glances and secrets hidden in the hearts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No intercession can turn falsehood into truth or God's truthful, just judgment into an unjust one.
rows.anchor: no one through his intercession or recommendation can turn God’s just decision into an unjust one.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The false deities have no authority to decide anything or speak for or against anyone.
rows.anchor: they will not have any authority whatsoever to decide any thing so that they would be able to speak against or in defence of someone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone sees and hears all, so no one else can have the right to judge.
rows.anchor: when the being who really sees and hears is God, who else can have the right to make a judgement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh are warned to travel and consider how stronger predecessor peoples were destroyed despite their numbers, architecture, culture, idols, and other resources; examples include ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Madyan.
rows.anchor: have they never journeyed through this land to see the fate met by their predecessor nations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term for greater might also includes greater size and greater numbers, making its pairing with traces of achievement apt.
rows.anchor: also encompasses the meaning of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traces of past peoples refer to cultural advances and architectural feats, often treated as marks of grandeur.
rows.anchor: refers to signs related to cultural advancements and architectural feats

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a faithless nation, such marks become signs of decline and tombs of its collective existence.
rows.anchor: if a nation is devoid of faith, then these signs become manifestations of its downfall and decadence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples were destroyed because they rejected clear signs brought by God's messengers while intoxicated by worldly power and success; once seized, they could not escape God.
rows.anchor: they did not pay any heed to the warnings sounded by their respective messenger. Finally, they were seized by the Almighty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can escape God's grasp, so He has no need to hasten; haste is needed only by one who fears the prey may escape.
rows.anchor: No one has the power to evade His grasp; so when no one is beyond His grasp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those seeking the Hereafter's harvest receive an increase in it and also whatever worldly provision God wills.
rows.anchor: those who strive for harvest in the Hereafter, God blesses their harvest of the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who seek only worldly life receive what God's wisdom entails here but have no share in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: those who are after this worldly life only and are heedless of the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section III follows the prophets' shared monotheistic message by rejecting any alternative religion fabricated by idolaters' deities, then points to remorse at Judgment and success through faith and righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: Now in the succeeding verses, it is being said that if the alleged deities of these idolaters have fabricated some other religion for them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who follow a fabricated religion will regret it at Judgment.
rows.anchor: people will feel remorse and sorrow for what they did

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success belongs to those who prepare for the Hereafter through faith and righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: only those people will succeed who will earn for it by professing faith and doing righteous deeds.

rows.claim: They allege that the Prophet calls them to the religion from a personal motive rather than concern for their welfare.
rows.anchor: it is because of a purely personal motive.

rows.claim: They object that the Prophet invents his discourse and falsely attributes it to God to inspire awe.
rows.anchor: whatever discourse the Prophet (sws) is presenting is concocted by him

rows.speaker: opponents of the Prophet
